whoIsThisFor.heading: Who is the B2B Commerce Administrator AP exam for?

personas.label: Salesforce admins managing B2B storefronts
personas.description: You look after a B2B Commerce store in Salesforce and want proof that you know how to set it up and run it.

personas.label: Implementation partners
personas.description: You build B2B stores for clients and need a credential that shows you know the setup end to end.

personas.label: Operations leads
personas.description: You own the online ordering channel for business buyers and want to understand how products, prices and buyers fit together.

examDifficulty.heading: Is the B2B Commerce Administrator AP Exam Hard?
examDifficulty.summary: It is a fair but strict exam. The topics are practical admin tasks, but the pass mark is high, so you need to know the setup steps well rather than roughly.
bullets: 75% to pass, which is 45 correct answers. That is higher than most Accredited Professional exams.
Setup order matters. Many questions are about what must be in place before a buyer can see a product or check out.
Hands-on helps a lot. If you have built a test store yourself, many questions will feel familiar.
examDifficulty.passRateGuidance: Build a store in a trial or sandbox org before the exam. Before you book. Aim for 85% or more on practice tests, since the pass mark leaves little room for error.

examFormat.heading: B2B Commerce Administrator AP Exam Format Explained
examFormat.intro: Accredited Professional exams are taken online. Here is what to expect:
examFormat.scenarioPercent: Most questions are short admin scenarios, such as a buyer who can't see a product or a price that looks wrong, and ask what to set up or fix.
bestWayToPass: Learn the chain from buyer to product: Buyer account, buyer group, entitlement policy, catalog and price book all have to line up.
Know when to rebuild the search index: Product and category changes don't show in the store until the index is rebuilt.
Understand checkout: Know the main checkout steps and where pricing, tax, shipping and inventory checks come in.
Practise in a real store: Create a buyer, give them access, and place a test order.

certificationCard.description: This exam tests how you set up and run a B2B Commerce store in Salesforce: stores, buyers, catalogs, prices, search and checkout. The exam is 60 scored questions in 90 minutes, with a 75% pass mark, weighted towards Salesforce B2B Commerce App and Storefront Deployment (20% each).

keyConcepts.h2: B2B Commerce Admin AP: Key Concepts for the Exam

blocks.heading: Store Setup & Storefront Configuration
blocks.body: A B2B store is created from the Commerce app and is built on an Experience Cloud site, which you design in Experience Builder. Each store has its own settings for currencies, languages, buyer access and checkout. The store is linked to one or more catalogs and to the buyer groups that can use it. Guest browsing can be turned on so visitors can see products before they log in, but buying still needs a buyer account. Keep a test store or sandbox to try changes before they reach buyers.

blocks.heading: Product Catalog & Pricing
blocks.body: Products live in a **catalog** organised into **categories**. A product can be simple or have variations, such as size and colour, set up with a variation parent and variation attributes. Prices come from **price books**, and each buyer group is assigned the price books it should use. If a buyer sees no price. Check that the product is in a price book linked to their buyer group. After changing products, categories or searchable fields, **rebuild the search index** so the changes appear in the store.

blocks.heading: Buyer Account & Contact Management
blocks.body: A business customer is an Account that has been **enabled as a buyer account**. Its contacts become **buyer users**, who are external users that log in to the store. Buyer accounts are added to **buyer groups**. Buyer groups are the key link: they get **entitlement policies**, which decide which products the buyers can see and buy, and price books, which decide what they pay. Changing access for many customers at once is done by changing the buyer group, not each account.

blocks.heading: Order Management & Checkout
blocks.body: Checkout takes the buyer from cart to order. Along the way the store checks inventory, works out prices, shipping and tax, and takes payment, often through integrations with outside systems. Once the order is placed it becomes an Order in Salesforce, and with Salesforce Order Management an **Order Summary** that tracks fulfilment, changes and returns. Buyers can reorder from their order history, and admins can set up approval steps or purchase limits where needed.

blocks.heading: Integration with Salesforce CRM
blocks.body: Because the store runs inside Salesforce, buyer accounts, contacts, orders and cases are the same records your sales and service teams use. Sales reps can see what a customer ordered online. Service agents can handle order questions as Cases. Reports and dashboards can combine online orders with the rest of the pipeline. Outside systems such as an ERP usually supply prices, stock and order status through integrations.

scenarioTips.h2: How to Pass the Salesforce B2B Commerce Administrator Accredited Professional Exam
scenarioTips.intro: Most questions are about why a buyer can't see or buy something, or how to set something up for many buyers at once. Trace the chain from buyer to product.

blocks.heading: Store Setup & Configuration
blocks.body: A store sits on an Experience Cloud site. Settings like currency, language and guest browsing are set per store.

blocks.heading: Product Catalog Management
blocks.body: Products go in catalogs and categories. After changes, rebuild the search index, or buyers won't see them.

blocks.heading: Buyer Groups & Entitlements
blocks.body: If a buyer can't see a product. Check the entitlement policy on their buyer group. If they can't see a price. Check the price book on the buyer group.

blocks.heading: Cart & Checkout Configuration
blocks.body: Checkout steps cover inventory, pricing, shipping, tax and payment. Each can call an outside system.

blocks.heading: Order Management Integration
blocks.body: Placed orders become Orders, and with Order Management, Order Summaries that track fulfilment and returns.

nextCertsAfter.heading: Next Certifications After This AP
nextCertsAfter.intro: Good next steps after B2B Commerce Admin:

sampleQuestions.question: A buyer logs in but can't see a new product line in the store. The products are in the catalog. What should the admin check first?
options: The entitlement policy on the buyer's buyer group
sampleQuestions.explanation: Entitlement policies decide which products a buyer group can see. If the products aren't in the policy, the buyer won't see them.
whyWrong: A wrong password would stop the login completely.
The theme changes how the store looks, not what products show.
Description length doesn't affect visibility.

sampleQuestions.question: A buyer can see a product but no price is shown. What is the most likely cause?
options: The search index is too new
The buyer has too many items in the cart
The product isn't in a price book assigned to the buyer's buyer group
sampleQuestions.explanation: Prices come from the price books linked to the buyer group. No matching price book entry means no price.
whyWrong: A recently rebuilt index isn't a problem.
Cart size doesn't hide prices.
Images don't affect prices.

sampleQuestions.question: The admin renamed several categories and added new products, but buyers still see the old names. What should the admin do?
options: Ask buyers to clear their cache
sampleQuestions.explanation: Store search and navigation use the search index. It must be rebuilt for product and category changes to appear.
whyWrong: Profiles don't control category names.
Recreating the store is unnecessary and loses setup.
The old names come from the index, not the buyers' browsers.

sampleQuestions.question: A company wants 300 customer accounts to get a new 10% price list. What is the most efficient way?
options: Assign the new price book to the buyer group those accounts belong to
Ask buyers to enter a discount code
sampleQuestions.explanation: Buyer groups let you change prices for many accounts at once by assigning a price book to the group.
whyWrong: Editing 300 accounts is slow and error-prone.
One store can serve many buyers.
A discount code relies on every buyer remembering it.

sampleQuestions.question: What must happen before a contact at a customer company can log in and place orders?
options: The contact must have a Sales Cloud licence
The contact must be a Salesforce admin
The account must be enabled as a buyer account and the contact must have a buyer user
The account must be marked as a competitor
sampleQuestions.explanation: Buyer access starts with a buyer account. Its contacts are then set up as external buyer users who can log in to the store.
whyWrong: Buyers don't need internal Sales Cloud licences.
Buyers are external users, not admins.
Competitor status has nothing to do with store access.

sampleQuestions.question: Visitors should be able to browse products before logging in; but only logged-in buyers can place orders. What should be turned on?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Guest browsing lets visitors see the catalog without logging in, while checkout still needs a buyer account.
whyWrong: A second store is unnecessary for this.
Self-registration creates accounts but doesn't allow browsing without login.
Opening all objects is a big security risk.

sampleQuestions.question: A T-shirt comes in three sizes and four colours. How should it be set up in the catalog?
options: A variation parent with variation attributes for size and colour
A separate category for each colour
One product with sizes in the description
sampleQuestions.explanation: Variations group the options under one parent, so buyers pick size and colour on a single product page.
whyWrong: Twelve separate products make browsing confusing.
Categories organise products. They don't create options.
Sizes in the description can't be selected or priced.

sampleQuestions.question: Which record links buyer accounts to the products they can see and the prices they pay?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Buyer groups hold the entitlement policies and price books that apply to their buyer accounts.
whyWrong: The theme controls look and feel.
The search index helps buyers find products, it doesn't control access.
Checkout handles buying, not visibility or pricing.

sampleQuestions.question: During checkout, the store must confirm that items are in stock in the company's ERP. Where does this fit?
options: The inventory check step in checkout, using an integration with the ERP
sampleQuestions.explanation: Checkout has a step for checking inventory, which can call the outside system for live stock levels.
whyWrong: Profiles control permissions, not stock.
A weekly report is far too late at checkout.
Descriptions can't check stock.

sampleQuestions.question: A sales rep wants to see what a customer has ordered through the B2B store. Where can they find it?
options: On the customer's Account in Salesforce, since store orders are Salesforce records
Only in a separate commerce system
sampleQuestions.explanation: The store runs in Salesforce, so orders are linked to the same Account records that reps use.
whyWrong: There is no need to ask, the data is in Salesforce.
Theme settings don't hold order data.
B2B Commerce runs inside Salesforce, not in a separate system.

sampleQuestions.question: After an order is placed, the team wants to track fulfilment, changes and returns. What should they use?
options: Salesforce Order Management with Order Summaries
sampleQuestions.explanation: Order Management creates an Order Summary that tracks the order through fulfilment, changes and returns.
whyWrong: Chatter is for collaboration, not order tracking.
A spreadsheet is manual and disconnected.
The cart is gone once the order is placed.

sampleQuestions.question: The store must sell in US dollars and euros. Where is this set?
options: In the store's currency settings, with price books for each currency
sampleQuestions.explanation: Stores can support several currencies, with prices coming from price books in each currency.
whyWrong: Product names don't control currency.
Passwords are unrelated.
The search index doesn't set currency.

sampleQuestions.question: An admin wants to change the layout of the store's home page without code. Which tool should they use?
sampleQuestions.explanation: B2B stores are built on Experience Cloud sites, and Experience Builder lets admins change pages with drag and drop.
whyWrong: Workbench is a utility for queries and API work.
Developer Console is for code.
Data Loader moves data.

sampleQuestions.question: A product should only be sold to buyers in the Healthcare buyer group. How should this be set up?
options: Add the product only to the entitlement policy used by the Healthcare buyer group
Remove the product from all price books
Put 'Healthcare only' in the product name
sampleQuestions.explanation: Entitlement policies control which buyer groups can see and buy each product.
whyWrong: Removing prices stops everyone buying it, including Healthcare.
A note in the name doesn't stop others buying it.
CSS only hides the product on screen. It can still be found.

sampleQuestions.question: Buyers often order the same items every month. Which feature saves them time?
options: Downloading the catalog as a PDF
Creating a new account each time
sampleQuestions.explanation: Buyers can reorder past orders from their order history, which adds the same items to the cart in one step.
whyWrong: A PDF doesn't place an order.
Calling service is slower and costs more.
New accounts add confusion and lose history.
